newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bayer not satisfied with generics business.
newsitem.headline: Bayer not satisfied with generics business.

text.p: German chemicals and drugs group Bayer AG said on Tuesday that it was not satisfied with its performance in the highly competitive generic drugs market.
"We are not satisfied with the generics (unit), the price pressure has become much harder," Walter Wenninger, Bayer board member for health sciences, told a news conference.
Generic drugs are prescription medications whose patent protection has lapsed.

Wenninger said price pressures are particularly intense in the United States. In Germany, where Bayer launced a separate generics group earlier this year, Wenninger said it was too early to say how the company is doing in that business.

Speaking about the drugs market in general, Wenninger said that sales in U.S. posted the strongest growth. On the other hand, sales in Japan, dented by a weaker yen as well as price cuts, were less pleasing, Wenninger said.
